menu Cost (tax included)

*Guideline/Standard body type

  • Face line (1~8cc)

Treatment details of fat dissolving injection

Lipolytic injection is a treatment that aims to reduce localized fat by injecting a drug into the subcutaneous fat layer of areas where fat is a concern. At our hospital, we use DEOLIPO, which contains deoxycholic acid. Deoxycholic acid acts on the cell membrane of fat cells, and the decomposed fat cells are gradually processed through the body's metabolic process, aiming to improve the contours of the face, upper arms, abdomen, thighs, etc.

Before the treatment, the doctor will check your fat deposits, skin condition, desired area to be treated, past medical history, allergies, and any medications you are currently taking. After marking and disinfecting the treatment area, the drug is injected into the subcutaneous fat layer in small amounts using a thin needle, depending on the thickness and area of ​​the fat. The amount of drug used depends on the area being treated and the amount of fat.

The treatment time varies depending on the area to be injected and the amount of drug. In some cases, the treatment can be completed in one treatment, but depending on the amount of fat removed and the desired result, we may recommend multiple treatments at certain intervals. There are individual differences in changes after treatment and the number of treatments required, and it is not a treatment for significant weight loss.

After the treatment, do not rub or put pressure on the injection site, and refrain from strenuous exercise, long baths, saunas, drinking alcohol, etc. for the period instructed by your doctor.

Risks and side effects of fat-dissolving injections

During the procedure, you may experience pain from the needle or irritation when the medication is injected. After the procedure, swelling, pain, redness, heat, itching, swelling, internal bleeding, numbness, tenderness, induration, and discomfort may occur. These symptoms usually subside over time, but the length of time they last varies from person to person.

Depending on the injection amount and how the drug spreads, there may be differences between the left and right sides, unevenness, sagging of the skin, or the inability to achieve the desired changes. Allergic reactions, hematomas, infections, abscesses, inflammation, ulcers, skin disorders, pigmentation, and skin necrosis may also occur.

In rare cases, blood vessels and nerves may be damaged, resulting in neuropathy such as decreased sensation, numbness, pain, and muscle weakness. If injected into the face, under the jaw, or around the neck, dysphagia such as lateralized expression, facial nerve damage, and difficulty swallowing may occur.

There are individual differences in how side effects appear. If you experience symptoms such as severe pain, swelling, discoloration of the skin, blisters, wounds, fever, or pus, please contact our hospital immediately.

Peeling treatment details

Peeling is a treatment that aims to improve skin turnover by applying an acidic agent to the skin and removing dead skin cells that have accumulated on the skin surface. It is used to treat skin problems such as clogged pores, acne, rough skin, dullness, and pigmentation.

Before treatment, your doctor will check your skin condition, check your treatment history, allergies, and any medications you are currently taking. After washing and washing your face to remove sebum and makeup, protect your eyes and mouth, and apply a peeling agent to the treatment area. After leaving it on for a certain period of time while checking the reaction of the skin, the drug is wiped off or neutralized and washed. After the treatment, prepare your skin with a moisturizer.

After treatment, the skin becomes more susceptible to irritation from UV rays and friction, so moisturizing and UV protection are necessary. The number of treatments and treatment intervals vary depending on the drug used, skin condition, and treatment purpose. In some cases, you may only receive one treatment, but depending on your condition, we may recommend multiple treatments at certain intervals.

MilanoRepeel treatment details

MilanoRepeel is a peeling treatment in which drugs containing multiple acids, mainly TCA (trichloroacetic acid), amino acids, vitamins, etc. are applied to the skin. The purpose is to remove dead skin cells from the skin surface, adjust skin turnover, and improve skin texture, roughness, dullness, pores, firmness, etc.

At our clinic, we perform treatments on the face, neck, and back of the hands. After checking the condition of your skin and the area to be treated, we will wash your face and cleanse to remove makeup and sebum. Mix the drug well, apply it to the treatment area, and check the skin reaction while letting it blend into the skin. Afterwards, wipe off the chemicals, cleanse and moisturize.

Milano Repeat Peel is a one-time treatment. Depending on your skin condition and treatment goals, we may recommend multiple treatments at regular intervals. The number and interval of treatments will vary from person to person, so your doctor will advise you during your consultation.

Peeling risks and side effects

During the treatment, you may experience tingling, pain, a feeling of heat, or hot flashes. After the treatment, redness, swelling, itching, dryness, a feeling of tightness, peeling, stinging, and scabbing may occur.

Depending on your skin condition and reaction to the drug, temporary worsening of acne or inflammation, pigmentation, depigmentation, blisters, burns, allergic reactions, etc. may occur. Symptoms may also be worsened by strong sunburn or friction.

MilanoRepeal risks and side effects

During the treatment, you may experience tingling, pain, a feeling of heat, or hot flashes. After the treatment, you may experience redness, swelling, itching, dryness, tightness, peeling, tingling, and scabs.

In rare cases, severe inflammation, blisters, burns, hyperpigmentation, depigmentation, and allergic reactions may occur. After the treatment, your skin will be more susceptible to irritation, so please be sure to moisturize your skin thoroughly, protect yourself from UV rays, and refrain from rubbing your skin or using harsh cosmetics.

There are individual differences in how side effects appear. If you experience severe pain, swelling, blisters, or long-lasting redness after your treatment, please contact our clinic immediately.

DOTT HAIR treatment details

DOTT HAIR is a drug treatment for thinning hair and hair loss caused by androgenetic alopecia (AGA). There are ``liquids'' that are applied directly to the scalp and ``tablets'' that are taken daily.We will prescribe a prescription after confirming your hair thinning condition, past medical history, medications you are taking, blood pressure, etc. during a medical examination.

DOTT HAIR (liquid)

DOTT HAIR Liquid is a topical medication containing 6.5% minoxidil and 0.05% finasteride. The aim is to stimulate hair growth with minoxidil, and suppress the production of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which causes AGA, with finasteride, thereby suppressing the progression of hair loss.

Normally, apply 1 mL at a time twice a day, in the morning and evening, to areas of the scalp where you are concerned about thinning hair, and blend it in with the pads of your fingers. After washing your hair, dry your hair and scalp thoroughly before using. Wash your hands thoroughly after use and be careful not to get it in your eyes or mouth. One 60mL bottle is enough for about 1 month.

DOTT HAIR (tablet)

DOTT HAIR tablets are oral medications containing 2.5mg of minoxidil and 0.65mg of finasteride, as well as vitamins, minerals, and amino acids. The aim is to suppress the progression of AGA with finasteride, while promoting hair growth with minoxidil.

In general, take 2 tablets once a day with water or lukewarm water. You can take this medicine before or after meals, but it is best to take it at the same time every day to keep the drug concentration in your body constant. One box contains 60 tablets, which is about a month's supply. The actual usage and dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical examination results and physical condition.

Since AGA is a progressive disease, treatment is continued for a certain period of time while checking for hair loss, hair condition, and side effects. The timing and degree of changes resulting from treatment vary from person to person, and not all patients will see the same results. Do not increase the dosage or stop taking or applying the medicine on your own; follow your doctor's instructions.

DOTT HAIR risks and side effects

Risks and side effects of DOTT HAIR (liquid)

Scalp rash, redness, itching, rash, dandruff, dryness, warmth, and pain may occur. You may also experience headaches, dizziness, chest pain, palpitations, increased heart rate, decreased blood pressure, sudden weight gain, and swelling of your limbs or face.

If the drug comes into contact with your face or other areas, the hair in those areas may become thicker. If it gets into your eyes, rinse immediately with water. If eye pain or redness persists, seek medical attention.

Risks and side effects of DOTT HAIR (tablet)

Palpitations, tachycardia, chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, light-headedness, headache, decreased blood pressure, swelling of the limbs and face, sudden weight gain, and hirsutism may occur. In rare cases, symptoms related to the heart or blood vessels may occur.

In addition, the effects of finasteride may cause decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, ejaculation dysfunction, decreased semen volume, breast swelling/tenderness, rash, liver dysfunction, and depressed mood. After starting treatment, you may experience a temporary increase in hair loss.

People with heart, kidney, or liver disease, high or low blood pressure, or those who are using other AGA drugs or antihypertensive drugs may not be able to receive treatment. DOTT HAIR for Men is a treatment for men. Not for use by women, minors, women who are or may become pregnant, or women who are breastfeeding.

There are individual differences in how side effects appear. If you experience chest pain, strong palpitations, difficulty breathing, sudden swelling, sudden weight gain, dizziness that makes you lose consciousness, etc., please discontinue use and promptly consult our hospital.

Contents, usage, and dosage of oral medications

At our hospital, a doctor will perform an examination and prescribe a prescription after confirming the patient's physical condition, symptoms, medical history, and medications he or she is currently taking. The following is the general usage and dosage for adults listed in the package insert of each drug. The actual dosage, number of doses, and prescription period will vary depending on the results of your medical examination. Be sure to follow the usage and dosage instructions given by your doctor.

Sinar

Cynar is an oral medicine containing ascorbic acid (vitamin C) and calcium pantothenate. In general, for adults, administer 1 to 3 tablets orally 1 to 3 times a day. The dosage may be increased or decreased depending on your age and symptoms.

Transamine

Transamine is an anti-plasmin drug whose active ingredient is tranexamic acid. The usual dose for adults is 750 to 2,000 mg of tranexamic acid per day, orally administered in 3 to 4 divided doses. The dosage may be increased or decreased depending on your age and symptoms.

Yubela

Yuvera is an oral medicine whose active ingredient is tocopherol acetate (vitamin E). The usual dose for adults is 50 to 100 mg orally 2 to 3 times a day. The dosage may be increased or decreased depending on your age and symptoms.

Haitiol

Hythiol is an oral medicine containing L-cysteine as an active ingredient. When used for skin diseases, the usual adult dose is 80mg of L-cysteine ​​administered orally 2 to 3 times a day. The dosage may be increased or decreased depending on your age and symptoms.

Vitadan

Vitadan is an oral medicine containing vitamin B1 derivatives, vitamin B2, vitamin B6, and vitamin B12. In general, for adults, take 1 to 2 tablets per day orally. The dosage may be increased or decreased depending on your age and symptoms.

Tathion

Tathion is an oral medication containing glutathione as an active ingredient. In general, for adults, administer 50 to 100 mg of reduced glutathione orally 1 to 3 times a day. The dosage may be increased or decreased depending on your age and symptoms.

Main risks and side effects of oral medications

Cynar risks and side effects

Stomach discomfort, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea may occur. Additionally, vitamin C may affect test results such as urine tests and fecal occult blood tests.

Transamine risks and side effects

Loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, heartburn, drowsiness, rash, and itching may occur. Convulsions may occur in rare cases in patients undergoing dialysis. People with thrombosis, those who are at risk of thrombosis, or those with decreased renal function may not be able to take this medicine or may need to make careful decisions.

Yuvera risks and side effects

Constipation, stomach discomfort, diarrhea, and rash may occur.

Risks and side effects of Hythiol

Nausea, diarrhea, dry mouth, and mild abdominal pain may occur.

Risks and side effects of Vitadan

Rash, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, stomach pain, stomach discomfort, abdominal bloating, dry mouth, diarrhea, insomnia, and frequent urination may occur. In addition, urine may turn yellow due to the effects of vitamin B2.

Tathion risks and side effects

Rash, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, and stomach pain may occur.

There are individual differences in how side effects appear. If you notice any changes in your physical condition or any worrisome symptoms after taking this medicine, please stop taking it or consult your doctor immediately.
